standard_prerequisites.name: The comparison map for the union of two opens satisfies the Mayer-Vietoris condition, so the induction principle applies
standard_prerequisites.use: Reduces the statement to quasi-compact opens and their unions.

standard_prerequisites.name: On an affine scheme a perfect or pseudo-coherent complex is represented by a bounded above complex of finite free modules, and a complex of finite tor dimension is described by a tor amplitude bound
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies the concrete representatives with which the colimit computation is performed in the affine case.

standard_prerequisites.name: The statement over the ring, which computes maps between the pulled back complexes as a colimit, is contained in the algebra chapter
standard_prerequisites.use: Finishes the affine case and hence the proof.

core_obligations: Introduce the condition that the canonical map from the colimit of the Hom groups on the approximations to the Hom group on the limit is an isomorphism for a given quasi-compact open, and record that it suffices to prove this condition for all quasi-compact opens (proof lines 7466-7472).

Verify the Mayer-Vietoris condition of the induction principle: if the condition holds on two opens and on their intersection then it holds on their union, which follows from the Mayer-Vietoris sequence for Hom in the derived category (proof lines 7472-7478).

Reduce to the affine case, where the objects can be described: in the first case the perfect complex is represented by a bounded above complex of finite free modules and the quasi-coherent complex is bounded below, and in the second case the pseudo-coherent complex is represented by finite free modules and the other complex has a tor amplitude bound (proof lines 7479-7500).

With those descriptions, translate the colimit of Hom groups into the corresponding statement over the rings of the system and conclude it from the algebra statement, which proves the condition in the affine case (proof lines 7500-7529).
proof_roadmap: Set up the condition and check the Mayer-Vietoris hypothesis (proof lines 7466-7478).
Reduce to affine schemes and describe the objects in both cases (proof lines 7479-7500).
Invoke the algebra statement to finish the affine case (proof lines 7500-7529).
